items.claim: A paint reference that resolves to nothing paints solid black instead of none
readStroke drops marker-start/mid/end on any element whose stroke is `none` or unset, though SVG draws them
A tspan's absolute or em `baseline-shift` is divided by the tspan's own font size, but `baselineShift` is in ems of the inherited size
A declaration CSS rejects overrides a valid one for stroke-width, font-size, dasharray, dashoffset, letter-spacing, markers and clip-path
`<marker refX="center">` (or right/bottom) without a viewBox resolves to 0
Marker children that are `display="none"` are drawn into the head
A mesh patch point written `x,` parses as `(x, 0)` instead of being rejected
A run whose stroke has zero width writes no stroke attributes, so its `<tspan>` takes the text's stroke
A namespaced meta element's child in another declared namespace is stored under its local name only, then written back in its parent's namespace
Every marker an import creates is registered globally and never released
The golden round-trip helper rounds tiny negatives to -0, which `toEqual` treats as different from 0
`<tspan>` that sets only stroke-width, dash, cap, join, or opacity loses the inherited paint
`<tspan stroke="inherit">` / `unset` comes out black with a warning
items.note: (same root cause as the line above: the run's stroke was read from the tspan's own attributes instead of its full cascade)

items.claim: `text: 'embed'` declares the substituted face under the wrong family name
`strokeDataFromSvg` drops `align`
Fit-clamp drop leaves a group's stroke and border unscaled
Golden round-trip helper ignores polygon `origin`
`dominant-baseline` is read only from the element's own attribute
Marker outline `stroke-width` ignores units
Absolute `baseline-shift` read as that many ems
items.note: One existing test expected `4px` to read as 4 ems with a warning; it now uses `4vw`, a unit that still can't be converted. The `supports.test.ts` sample was changed the same way.

items.claim: `<text>`-level `baseline-shift` dropped from `<tspan>` runs
Fit-clamp turns an `INHERIT` stroke into an object of its characters
items.note: (same commit as the group-stroke fix, which B reported in the same finding)

items.claim: Keyword values validated without regard to case but read with it
`<pattern>` `<image>` read without checking its `transform` or `preserveAspectRatio`
items.note:
A transformed image now drops to the unsupported-pattern warning.
  - An explicit `preserveAspectRatio` other than `none` now warns and still reads stretched, matching how a bare `<image>` is handled.
  - A pattern image with no `preserveAspectRatio` still reads as an image fill with no warning. An existing test covers exactly that case for other editors' bitmap patterns, so I kept it. I didn't treat this as a new behavior call or add anything to `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: `roundTrip` helper drops most node fields before comparing
items.note: It now compares every field, with geometry in world coordinates. All golden fixtures still pass.

items.claim: Fit-clamp leaves a framed text leaf's `padding` unscaled

A run's stroke replaces the node's stroke, but the `<tspan>` it was written as inherited the node's cap, join, dash, miter limit, and opacity, so a browser drew it differently from the canvas. The writer now writes those properties at their initial values
items.note: The old `roundtrip.text.test.ts` expectation that a tspan "inherits nothing else" contradicted how SVG draws it, so I updated it.

items.claim: `isDeclarationHonored` matched `inherit` only in lowercase
